text.p: Bonds closed at session highs for the short to medium term part of the curve but the longer end failed to keep pace with Spain and the Bunds, traders said.
The main factor restraining market enthusiasm is the 15 billion escudos of 10-year bonds being offered by the Credit Institute on Monday, they said.
The Bank of Portugal's 30 basis point cut in rates, which took analysts by surprise, lifted the short to medium bonds.
Analysts said that the cut meant that the Credit Institute should have little problem in placing the full 15 billion escudos of three-year bonds it will also offer on Monday.
"The curve steepened and there were final-users coming into the market to buy up to the medium-term bonds," said one trader.
"Nevertheless, the curve has room to steepen further," added another, adding that despite the rally, the spread with the two-year Bonos was still around 20 basis points.
The spread between the two-year and the 10-year Portuguese bonds widened to 110 basis points from 103 at Thursday's close.
"The market closed strong but the potential for further gains remains. And the great beneficiary is going to be the state," said one trader.
